subject: Discovery recap + quick check on timeline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@neoanalytics.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@neoanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + next step suggestion

Hi Jamie / Alex —

Great to meet you both earlier. Quick recap from today’s call and a proposed next step so we keep momentum: 

What we heard
- NeoAnalytics needs predictable burst throughput for ad-hoc analytics summaries (3–6k tokens/req), plus privacy controls for customer data ingestion.
- Top priorities: latency SLAs for interactive UX, audit logs for compliance, and price predictability for pilot capacity.

What Redwood recommends (short list)
- Start with a 6-week pilot on Dedicated (reserved pool, single-region) to validate throughput and end-to-end latency.
- Enable prefix caching for common prompts and a standard KV cache policy to reduce token cost.
- Baseline metrics we’ll measure: p95 latency, tokens-per-user, and cost-per-1k-requests.

Proposed next step
- Pilot kickoff: 2-week technical onboarding + 4-week evaluation window.
- Can your infra lead share a preferred week for a 60-min kick-off (we’re flexible week of Apr 19)?

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap-neoanalytics.pdf (PDF, 120KB); mutual-action-plan.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

If that plan looks reasonable I can draft a short MOU and calendar the kickoff.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@neoanalytics.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@neoanalytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next step suggestion — checking in

Jamie —

Wanted to bump this in case it slipped through. Quick question: is this pilot still something you’re planning to prioritize in Q2? If priorities shifted, totally understand — a one-line update (yes / push to Q3 / not a fit) helps me and the team plan.

If you’re still interested, we can tentatively pencil in Apr 26 for a kickoff and I’ll send a short MOU for review. If you'd rather I loop back later, tell me a month that works and I’ll follow up then.

Short and simple appreciated.

—Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@neoanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Quick check — fit feedback?

Jamie —

Two-line ask: can you share whether this is a) definitely worth pursuing, b) interesting but not a priority this quarter, or c) not a fit?

If it’s (a), we’ll send a kickoff invite + a 1-page MOU. If (b), when should I follow up (month/quarter)? If (c), any feedback on why (concerns on pricing, data residency, scope) would be super helpful.

No pressure — want to make sure we’re not pinging you unnecessarily.

Thanks in advance,
Karthik

From: Jamie Park <jamie@neoanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@neoanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + quick check on timeline

Hey Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and follow-ups. Short answer: we love Redwood’s approach but have to pause pilot conversations until our Q3 budget cycle is finalized. So option (b).

Why: procurement sign-off and budget timing are the blockers — nothing technical. Please circle back mid-June and I’ll prioritize a quick kickoff then if our numbers look good.

Appreciate the succinct plan and attachments — they helped us frame internal ask.

Best,
Jamie
